TI Comparing ondansetron versus phenylephrine in reduce the incidence of
   hypotension after spinal anesthesia in cesarean section
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Cesarean section; hypotension; ondansetron; phenylephrine
ID MANAGEMENT
AB BACKGROUND: Spinal anesthesia is the method of choice for cesarean section (CS). This method poses risks such as maternal hypotension. Measures such as prescribing appropriate preventative medications can be an important strategy in the prevention and treatment of hypotension in mothers. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This quasi-experimental study was conducted at Arash Hospital, Tehran University of Medical Sciences, on 110 patients undergoing CS under spinal anesthesia. Then, patients who met the necessary conditions were randomly divided into one of two groups: ondansetron (n = 55) and phenylephrine (n = 55). After spinal anesthesia, one group received an intravenous dose of 100 micrograms of phenylephrine and the other group received 4 mg of ondansetron. During the procedure, the patient's blood pressure and heart rate were measured every 2 minutes for 20 minutes and then every 5 minutes until the end of the procedure. Data were collected using a researcher-made questionnaire that included demographic information. A P value < 0.05 will be considered significant. RESULTS: The mean age of all participants was 30.08 years, with a standard deviation of 5.90 years. Nausea occurred in 21 of the 110 participants (19.09%) during the surgical procedure. It was more common in the phenylephrine group, affecting 14 patients (25.45%), compared to only 7 patients (12.73%) in the ondansetron group (P = 0.089). Vomiting was a relatively rare event, occurring in only 4 participants (3.64%) across both groups. Of these, 3 cases (5.45%) were in the phenylephrine group, while only 1 case (1.82%) occurred in the ondansetron group (P = 0.308). CONCLUSION: The findings revealed that while both agents were effective in managing maternal hemodynamics during surgery, ondansetron was associated with a significantly lower need for repeat antiemetic administration and reduced nausea and vomiting without increasing the risk of hypotension or bradycardia. Therefore, this finding may be useful for clinical practice and further studies.

TI Determinants of inflammatory and adipokine biomarkers in obese young
   women: The role of skeletal muscle and lifestyle factors in Indonesia
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Adiponectin; cardiovascular risk; C-reactive protein; inflammation;
   interleukin-6; obesity; skeletal muscle
AB BACKGROUND: Obesity and cardiovascular diseases (CVD) are major public health concerns in Indonesia, especially among women who face a higher risk of obesity-related complications due to biological and lifestyle factors. Chronic low-grade inflammation, involving markers such as interleukin-6 (IL-6), high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP), and adiponectin (ADP), plays a crucial role in linking obesity to CVD. AIM: This study aimed to examine the association of sociodemographic, body composition, dietary intake, and physical activity factors with plasma IL-6, hs-CRP, and ADP levels in obese young adult women. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted among obese women in Bandung City, Indonesia. Thirty-eight women aged 18-25 years with body fat >35% were selected through purposive sampling. Anthropometric measurements (weight, height, waist/hip circumference, body composition) were taken using calibrated tools. Dietary intake was assessed through two 24-h recalls (weekday and weekend), and physical activity was recorded using a structured questionnaire. Inflammatory and adipokine biomarkers (IL-6, hs-CRP, ADP) were analyzed from fasting blood samples using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay kits. All tools were standardized and validated. Bivariate analysis (Chi-square test) identified candidate variables (P < 0.25) for multivariate logistic regression. Multiple linear regression was used to determine independent predictors of biomarker levels. RESULTS: Most participants had low energy intake and high fat consumption. No significant associations were found between the studied variables and IL-6 or hsCRP levels. However, lower education and decreased skeletal muscle and leg muscle mass were significantly associated with reduced ADP levels (P < 0.001). In multivariate analysis, leg skeletal muscle was the only significant predictor of ADP levels (P < 0.001) supporting the hypothesis that muscle mass, particularly in the lower limbs, influences anti-inflammatory adipokine levels. Besides, there is high pulse as a predictor of hsCRP level (P = 0.027). CONCLUSIONS: Leg skeletal muscle mass is a key determinant of ADP levels in obese young women, while pulse for hsCRP. This emphasizes the importance of strength-focused interventions to reduce cardiometabolic risk. These findings support health policy benchmarks that promote equitable access to physical activity and nutrition education, particularly for populations with lower educational attainment.

TI Vision-restricted dual-task training as a novel intervention to improve
   cognitive performance and quality of life in type 2 diabetes: A
   randomized controlled trial
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Cognitive dysfunction; dual-task performances; physical therapy
   modalities; quality of life; type 2 diabetes mellitus
AB BACKGROUND: Cognitive decline has been associated with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), a chronic metabolic disease marked by hyperglycemia brought on by decreased insulin production and resistance. In people with type 2 diabetes, cognitive motor dual-task blindfold training (CMDBT) supports gains in both cognitive and motor functioning by activating procedural memory areas, including the cerebellum, supplementary motor area, premotor cortex, and basal ganglia. MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this randomized controlled experiment, 62 individuals with a diagnosis of type 2 diabetes participated. An experimental group (n = 31) received CMDBT, whereas the control group (n = 31) was given conventional physiotherapy training. Using the primary outcome measures of Montreal Cognitive Assessment scale and Mini-mental State Examination and the secondary outcome measures of WHO BREF (physical domain) and WHO Qol-BREF (psychological domain), the baseline cognitive performance and quality of life were evaluated. RESULTS: The statistical study revealed both intervention-enhanced cognitive function and psychological wellbeing over time (P < 0.001). CMDBT produced greater cognitive improvement than CVPT, with a large effect size (Cohen's d = 0.85 post-test, 0.88 at follow-up) and significant P values (P = 0.003). Psychological quality of life improved in both groups, with no significant between-group differences (P = 0.315), indicating comparable efficacy. CONCLUSION: Cognitive-motor dual-task training is more successful than conventional physiotherapy programs at enhancing cognitive function in T2DM patients. These findings suggest CMDBT could be integrated into structured diabetic rehabilitation policies to reduce cognitive decline, aligned with global health initiatives promoting nonphamacological interventions.

TI Social jetlag and related circadian factors among medical students: A
   brief report of prevalence, contributing factors, and health effects
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Circadian rhythm; education; medical; sleep quality; sleep wake
   disorders; students
ID SLEEP; CHRONOTYPE
AB Social jetlag (SJL)-the misalignment between circadian rhythms and social schedules-is increasingly recognized among students, especially in medicine, where heavy workloads and irregular hours threaten sleep and functioning. This brief report mapped current evidence on the prevalence, factors, and outcomes of SJL in medical students. The review followed the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) methodology for scoping reviews. A three-step search strategy was applied across PubMed, Scopus, Embase, and Google Scholar from January 2015 to July 2025. Eligible studies included undergraduate or graduate medical students and examined SJL, chronotype, or circadian disruption in relation to academic, mental health, or lifestyle outcomes. Data extraction used a piloted form capturing study characteristics, population details, SJL definitions and measures, prevalence estimates, and outcomes. Findings were summarized descriptively, with study selection shown in a PRISMA-ScR flow diagram. Nineteen studies across four continents (Asia, Europe, North America, and Africa) were included. Chronotype distribution (15 studies) showed 15.64% morning, 58.37% intermediate, and 25.87% evening types. Reported or derived SJL (six studies) ranged from 1 h 12 min to 3 h 23 min. Eveningness was consistently associated with poor sleep quality, anxiety, depression, and unhealthy lifestyle behaviors, while evidence for academic performance effects was mixed. Overall, research on SJL in medical students is heterogeneous in definitions, measures, and outcomes, limiting comparability. Nonetheless, findings suggest eveningness and greater SJL are linked to adverse sleep and mental health. Future studies should apply standardized tools, clearer definitions, and broader language inclusion to inform interventions in medical education.

TI Relationship between psychological distress and turnover among nurses,
   the moderating role of self-growth
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Nursing workforce; psychological distress; self-growth; turnover
   intention
ID BURNOUT
AB BACKGROUND:The nursing profession faces significant stressors, leading to psychological distress, which can increase turnover intentions. Understanding the interplay between these factors and the role of self-growth is crucial for improving nurse retention.MATERIALS AND METHODS:This descriptive correlational study involved 232 registered nurses in Oman, recruited via convenience sampling from various healthcare facilities. Participants were eligible if they held a nursing diploma or higher, had at least six months of experience, and were proficient in English. Data were collected through an online survey distributed via social media platforms in March 2025, utilizing standardized instruments to measure psychological distress (K10), self-growth (PGIS), and turnover intention (TIS). It is recommended that tailored interventions, such as mentorship and stress management programs, be adopted to enhance resilience and job satisfaction. Supporting nurses' well-being and development is seen as vital for reducing turnover and improving patient care. Healthcare environments should be prioritized to foster self-growth and reduce distress, with structured programs proposed to benefit nurses and improve overall care quality.

TI Barriers and facilitators to self-management in chronic kidney disease
   patients undergoing hemodialysis: Insights from a qualitative study
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Kidney disease; nurses; renal dialysis; self-management
AB BACKGROUND:Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a global health challenge, with many patients dependent on hemodialysis (HD) for survival. Although HD prolongs life, it presents significant physical, psychological, and social difficulties, complicating self-management which is a vital aspect of CKD care. Self-management involves addressing symptoms, adhering to treatments, and managing psychosocial impacts. This study investigates barriers and facilitators of self-management in HD patients to inform care improvements.MATERIALS AND METHODS:A qualitative content analysis captured the experiences of 15 participants, including HD patients, family caregivers, and nurses from two Iranian hospitals. Purposive sampling ensured diverse perspectives. Data were collected via 17 semi-structured interviews and analyzed using Graneheim and Lundman's five-step framework.RESULTS:Key factors influencing self-management were categorized into four domains with eight subcategories. Patient-related factors included psychological challenges (depression, anxiety, denial, and cognitive impairments) and physical complications (comorbidities and side effects). Family and social support played critical roles, with emotional, informational, and financial support as facilitators, while socioeconomic constraints and stigma posed barriers. Healthcare system inefficiencies, such as inadequate education, limited resources, and poor interprofessional collaboration, were impediments, though informal and non-governmental organizations provided some mitigation. Daily life challenges, including difficulty organizing routines, balancing responsibilities, and maintaining social roles, highlighted the need for tailored interventions.CONCLUSION:Psychological, social, and systemic factors shape self-management in HD patients. Addressing barriers like inadequate education, emotional distress, and resource limitations while leveraging family support is crucial for enhancing patients' ability to manage their condition effectively.

TI Diagnostic and prognostic role of platelet indices in pre-eclampsia:
   Insights from a hospital-based study in Eastern part of India
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Biomarkers; maternal health; mean platelet volume; platelet distribution
   width; platelet indices; preeclampsia
ID HYPERTENSIVE DISORDERS; THROMBOCYTOPENIA; PREGNANCY; COUNT; WIDTH
AB BACKGROUND:Preeclampsia remains a major cause of maternal morbidity and mortality, characterized by hypertension and signs of organ dysfunction, including thrombocytopenia. Platelet indices such as mean platelet volume (MPV), platelet distribution width (PDW), plateletcrit (PCT), and platelet-large cell ratio (P-LCR) are emerging as potential biomarkers for preeclampsia severity and progression. To assess the association between platelet indices and preeclampsia among pregnant women attending antenatal care at a private healthcare facility in Bhubaneswar, Odisha.MATERIALS AND METHODS:A hospital-based prospective case-control study was conducted, including pregnant women diagnosed with preeclampsia (both mild and severe) and normotensive controls. Platelet indices were measured at the time of delivery and compared across groups. Statistical analysis included ANOVA and post hoc test for group comparisons and for relationship between platelet indices and disease severity. ROC curve analysis for diagnostic performance.RESULTS:A significant decrease in platelet count was observed in pre-eclamptic women compared to normotensive controls (mean platelet count: 2.38 +/- 0.44 & times; 103/& micro;l in normotensive, 2.14 +/- 0.47 & times; 103/& micro;l in mild preeclampsia, and 1.90 +/- 0.312 & times; 103/& micro;l in severe preeclampsia). In contrast, platelet indices such as MPV, PDW, PCT, and P-LCR were elevated in preeclampsia, with levels increasing in proportion to disease severity, except for PCT, which showed an inconsistent pattern. ROC analysis demonstrated that PDW (AUC: 0.622, P = 0.004), PCT (AUC: 0.712, P = 0.01), and MPV (AUC: 0.678, P = 0.01) had diagnostic significance, suggesting their potential role in predicting disease severity.CONCLUSION:Platelet indices, particularly PDW, MPV, and PCT, are significantly associated with preeclampsia and its severity. Incorporating these markers into routine antenatal screening could aid in early risk stratification. However, further multicenter studies and longitudinal follow-ups are recommended to establish standardized diagnostic cut-offs.

TI Factors associated with alcohol use and dependence among youth in Kolar
   district, India: A cross-sectional study
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Alcohol use; hazardous drinking; public health; risk factors; youth
   health
ID NONCOMMUNICABLE DISEASES; PREVENTION
AB BACKGROUND:This study aims to examine the prevalence and factors associated with alcohol use and alcohol dependence among youth in Kolar district, Karnataka, India.MATERIALS AND METHODS:A cross-sectional analysis was conducted using data from the Youth Health and Behavior Surveillance Survey (2021-2022) with 5,072 youth aged 15-30 years. Alcohol use was assessed using the WHO AUDIT score, categorizing participants into low-risk, hazardous, and dependent users. Descriptive and multivariate ordinal logistic regression analyses were performed to identify significant associations.RESULTS:The study found that 6.6% of youth were current alcohol users. Among these users, 21.8% engaged in hazardous use and 11% met criteria for alcohol dependence. This translates to a prevalence of 1.4% for hazardous use and 0.7% for alcohol dependence in the total population. Factors significantly associated with higher alcohol use included youth aged 26-30 years (adjusted odds ratio [AOR] = 5.5, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 2.7-10.7), current smokeless tobacco use (AOR = 3.2, 95% CI: 2.0-5.1), smoking (AOR = 7.7, 95% CI: 4.8-12.3), and smokeless tobacco dependence (AOR = 3.2, 95% CI: 1.4-7.1), consumption of burgers/pasta (AOR = 3.9, 95% CI: 1.7-8.9) and carbonated drinks (AOR = 1.5, 95% CI: 1.0-2.3), engagement in premarital/extramarital sexual relationships (AOR = 6.4, 95% CI: 3.2-12.9), experiencing physical violence (AOR = 5.1, 95% CI: 2.5-10.3), suicidal behaviors (AOR = 7.7, 95% CI: 2.2-25.9), and having peers who drink alcohol (AOR = 6.8, 95% CI: 4.6-10.2). Conversely, protective factors included being unemployed, engaging in free-time activities, and migrant status.CONCLUSION:The study highlights the complex interplay of sociodemographic, behavioral, and social factors influencing alcohol use patterns among youth and underscores the need for targeted interventions in this population.

TI Empowering dental students: A quasi-experimental study on disability
   awareness through the EQUALISED program

LA English
DT Article
DE Dental; dentists; disabled persons; feedback; schools; students; surveys
   and questionnaires
AB BACKGROUND: Persons with disabilities (PWDs) face significant barriers to accessing equitable dental care, primarily due to dentists' insufficient training. The Equality in Special Care Dentistry (EQUALISED) program aims to empower dental students with better understanding in providing dental care for PWDs. This study evaluates the program's impact on dental students' knowledge and awareness toward PWDs. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Using a quasi-experimental pretest-post-test design, knowledge and feedback among students at Universitas Airlangga were assessed after the program. Students also provided positive feedback, particularly valuing the real-life experiences shared by PWDs. CONCLUSIONS: The EQUALISED program significantly improved students' disability knowledge and awareness, supporting inclusive care goals aligned with health equity policies. Embedding such training into dental curricula can reduce oral health disparities and foster empathetic dentists.

TI Teachers' voices on sexuality in adolescents with intellectual
   disabilities: A phenomenological study
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Adolescent; intellectual disability; perception; sexuality
ID DEVELOPMENTAL-DISABILITIES; SEX-EDUCATION
AB BACKGROUND:Sexuality in adolescents with intellectual disabilities is a topic that remains largely unexplored due to prejudices, stigmas, exclusion, and deficient attention in sexual education. This study aimed to analyze teachers' perceptions and experiences regarding the sexual development of adolescents with intellectual disabilities.MATERIALS AND METHODS:A phenomenological study was conducted using an inductive content analysis method. Eight teachers from a special education center in Lima, Peru were intentionally selected and interviewed in depth. The data were interpreted, segmented into codes for a more specific analysis, and subsequently grouped into subthemes that allowed the categories to be defined.RESULTS:The findings of this study were grouped into two main categories: 1) Perceptions on the sexuality of adolescents with intellectual disabilities: indifferent sexual maturation process, predominance of hypersexual behaviors, considerations on sexual activity and the use of contraceptives, and the influence of family and school in constructing gender identity and sexual orientation; and 2) Experiences in approaching sexuality: the importance of comprehensive sex education, family involvement in supporting affective relationships, and including specialized professionals to adequately manage inappropriate behaviors.CONCLUSION:Teachers recognize their fundamental role in educating adolescents with intellectual disabilities. Their perceptions highlight the importance of applying a comprehensive approach to regulating sexual expressions. Their experiences demonstrate the necessity of implementing educational strategies that include specialized professionals.

TI Validity and reliability of the persian adapted version of the labor
   pain relief attitude questionnaire for pregnant women (P-LPRAQ-p)
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Attitude; Iran; labor pain; patient-controlled; pregnant women
ID EPIDURAL ANALGESIA; ADAPTATION; MANAGEMENT; KNOWLEDGE; SCALE
AB BACKGROUND: Labor pain, as one of the inevitable pains among women, is generally tolerable for most women. The present study aimed to assess the cultural adaption and psychometric adequacy of the Labor Pain Relief Attitude Questionnaire (LPRAQ) for pregnant women. MATERIALS AND METHOD: This psychometric study was conducted in four distinct phases. The first and second phases involved the forward-backward translation followed by necessary modifications, and the third phase focused on the content and face validity. In the fourth phase, construct validity (CV) and reliability were examined. CV was evaluated using confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) and concurrent validity through previously validated and reliable measurement instruments. The mean LPRAQ-p scores were compared across different groups in terms of age, spouse's age, education level, planning for pregnancy, number of pregnancies and childbirths, depression and distress, history of analgesia use, and delivery mode. A higher P-LPRAQ score indicated a greater willingness to seek labor pain relief. RESULTS: A total of 355 pregnant women who sought medical care in Tehran during 2022 were studied. During the face and content validity assessment, all six items of the instrument were retained. CFA of six items with two factors showed a good model fit index (X2/df < 5, (Comparative Fit Index) CFI = 0.91, (Normed Fit Index) NFI = 0.880.01, (Root Mean Square Error of Approximation) RMSEA = 0.04). The questionnaire also exhibited good convergent validity with (Tilburg Pregnancy Distress-negative -negative affect)TPDS-NA and Edinburg depression questionnaire (P < 0.05). Additionally, significant difference in the mean P-LPRAQ-p scores was observed in terms of the age, education level, spouse's age, employment status, mode of delivery, depression, and distress level (P < 0.001). CONCLUSION: The P-LPRAQ is a brief, concise, and straightforward questionnaire demonstrating optimal validity and reliability, making it a suitable tool for assessing pregnant women's attitudes toward labor pain relief.

TI Effectiveness of memory enhancement techniques vs. conventional teaching
   on schizophrenia for nursing students
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Decision-making; effectiveness; knowledge; nursing students;
   schizophrenia
AB BACKGROUND: Nursing students face several challenges in learning about schizophrenia, primarily due to the disorder's complexity. Additionally, limited hands-on clinical experience leaves students less equipped and lacking decision-making skills. The emotional strain of managing severe mental health issues adds anxiety and stress, further complicating their learning. The aim is to compare the effectiveness of memory enhancement techniques (MET) based teaching and conventional teaching regarding schizophrenia in terms of knowledge and decision-making ability among nursing students. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A quasi-experimental study was conducted using a nonequivalent control group pre- and post-test design on 74 nursing students studying in the 6(th) semester at selected nursing colleges in Ambala, Haryana. MET-based teaching was administered to the experimental group (n = 37) while the comparison group (n = 37) received Conventional teaching. Data were analyzed by using Parametric tests. RESULTS: At the end of the intervention, the post-test knowledge scores of nursing students in the MET group were significantly higher than the Conventional teaching group (P < 0.01). The decision-making ability significantly improved at the end of the intervention in the MET group than the Conventional group. CONCLUSION: Both teaching strategies were effective in enhancing the knowledge of nursing students regarding schizophrenia. However, MET-based teaching was more effective in enhancing the knowledge and decision-making ability of nursing students. The conventional teaching was found to be ineffective in improving the decision-making ability.

TI Teaching surgical instruments with a touch of play: A comparative study
   of Kahoot and Crossword puzzles as fun formative assessments for
   operating room nursing students
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Crossword puzzle; formative assessment; Kahoot; knowledge
AB BACKGROUND:This study aims to investigate the impact of collaborative Kahoot and Crossword puzzles as formative assessment tools on the knowledge, satisfaction, and motivation of operating room nursing students regarding posterior lumbar interbody fusion instrumentation. MATERIALS AND METHODS:In this quasiexperimental study, 40 operating room nursing students from the 6th and 8th semesters at Ardabil University of Medical Sciences were randomly assigned to two intervention groups. Two face-to-face sessions were conducted, and at the end of each session, collaborative formative assessment of students was conducted using two methods: one group used the Kahoot platform, while the other completed paper-based Crossword puzzles. For data collection, a researcher-developed knowledge test (pretest and post-test), Motivation for Cooperative Learning Strategies questionnaire, and a researcher-developed satisfaction questionnaire were used. RESULTS:There was no statistically significant difference in demographic variables and mean knowledge scores of the pretest between the Kahoot and Crossword puzzle groups (P > 0.05). The mean knowledge scores of the post-test were significantly higher than the mean pretest scores in both groups (P < 0.0001). In addition, the two groups had no significant difference in post-test scores (P > 0.05). However, the mean scores of satisfaction (P = 0.020) and motivation (P < 0.0001) were significantly higher in the Kahoot group compared with the Crossword puzzle group. CONCLUSION:Kahoot and Crossword puzzles are effective for formative assessment and feedback, enhancing operating room nursing students' knowledge. However, Kahoot significantly increases motivation, satisfaction, and engagement, offering dynamic learning experiences compared with Crossword puzzles.

TI Knowledge, attitude, and practice of infection control in a dental
   hospital among dental students and practicing dentists-A cross-sectional
   questionnaire study
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Infection control; dental infection control; sterilization; and
   disinfection
AB BACKGROUND: Infection control is an essential element in dental practice to avoid cross-contamination and safeguard patients and healthcare workers. Successful infection control depends on adequate knowledge, attitude, and practice (KAP) among dental practitioners. OBJECTIVE: This cross-sectional study was conducted to evaluate the Knowledge, Attitude, and Practice of infection control among dental students and practicing dentists in Puducherry, India. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A validated and structured questionnaire was filled out by 370 respondents, comprising dental undergraduates, postgraduates, and dentists in practice. Statistical analysis was done using SPSS version 16, and the Chi-square tests evaluating associations among the study variables. RESULTS: The survey showed major knowledge gaps, where only 3.5% of the participants had sufficient knowledge, and 50% lacked proper understanding. Attitude was found to be largely positive (47.3%), and practice was assessed as good among 63.5% of the respondents. Female respondents showed significantly better knowledge (P < 0.05) than their male counterparts. Practicing dentists scored the best for attitude and practice, whereas undergraduates recorded the worst knowledge. Spearman's rho correlation revealed a positive correlation between knowledge, attitude, and practice (P < 0.05). CONCLUSION: These findings highlight a critical need for improved infection control training among dental students and early-career professionals. Regular, comprehensive infection control education, coupled with periodic assessments, is essential for enhancing the overall safety and quality of dental care.

TI An exploratory study on the use of the self-directed learning,
   self-video recording, peer-to-peer review, and Direct feedback model to
   enhance clinical skills among medical students in Southern Thailand
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Clinical competence; feedback; medical education; self-directed
   learning; Thailand; video recording
AB BACKGROUND: Regional teaching hospitals in Southern Thailand must train large student cohorts despite limited faculty and heavy clinical workloads. We explored whether a composite Self-directed learning, Self-video recording, Peer-to-peer review, and Direct feedback (SSPD) model can strengthen core clinical skills under these constraints. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A quasi-experimental one-group pretest-post-test study was conducted among n = 49 clinical-year medical students from Surat Thani and Maharaj Nakhon Si Thammarat Hospitals (March to September 2024). Students completed a four-station Objective Structured Clinical Examination (OSCE) covering history taking, physical examination, procedural skills, and patient counseling both before and after a four-component SSPD intervention. The primary outcome was the change in OSCE scores; secondary outcomes were learner satisfaction and frequency of video use. Mean differences were analyzed with paired-sample t-tests (alpha = 0.05), and effect sizes were expressed as Cohen's d with 95% confidence intervals (CI). RESULTS: Significant gains were observed in history taking (Delta = 9.84 +/- 15.39; 95% CI: 5.42-14.26; d = 0.64; P < 0.001), physical examination (Delta = 16.37 +/- 19.08; 95% CI: 10.89-21.85; d = 0.86; P < 0.001), and patient counseling (Delta = 38.20 +/- 18.71; 95% CI: 32.83-43.57; d = 2.04; P < 0.001). Procedural skills showed no meaningful change (Delta = 0.06 +/- 17.51; 95% CI: -4.97-5.09; d approximate to 0.00; P = 0.981). Learners reported high satisfaction with self-directed learning and self-video recording components; 51% reviewed their videos. CONCLUSIONS: Despite the absence of a control group, medium-to-large effect sizes in three of four skill domains suggest the SSPD model is a feasible, scalable option for resource-limited clinical settings. Controlled trials should confirm these findings and determine long-term outcomes.

TI The Evolution of Women's Presence in Higher Education: An Underexplored
   Path
SO DEBATE UNIVERSITARIO
LA Spanish
DT Article
DE woman; university; evolution; history; trajectory
AB Throughout the history of the university system, women's presence in Higher Education has evolved alongside changes in women's representation in society and the objectification of women in science. In Argentina, from the exceptionality of their presence in university institutions to the current mass participation, women attending higher education is a recent phenomenon in historical terms. Women's opportunity to study has meant not only access to academic institutions but also the assumption of professional roles that were not always envisioned for them in the society of their time. This situation has led to complex processes marked by invisibility, tensions, and resistance. Based on a corpus compiled for this work, which includes a bibliographic survey and articles published in academic journals and university digital magazines, this work reviews women's participation in university education from its origins, then focuses on the Argentine university system, intertwining female participation with the system's historical context. The meta-analysis in the conclusions reveals that, while progress has been positive, the voices in the analyzed works still reveal that there are paths yet to be trodden.

TI The effect of educational intervention using behavioral pain scale to
   diagnose pain and relief care in patients admitted to the intensive care
   unit
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Behavioral Pain Scale; educational; intensive care unit; pain; pain
   measurement
ID CRITICALLY-ILL; POSTOPERATIVE PAIN; ADULT PATIENTS; MANAGEMENT;
   BARRIERS; NURSES; FACILITATORS; KNOWLEDGE
AB BACKGROUND:Considering that more than half of the patients hospitalized in the intensive care unit (ICU) experience pain, for this reason, diagnosis, management, and relief of pain are very important in this department.MATERIALS AND METHODS:In this intervention study, nurses working in the ICU were included and the study educational intervention was held in the field of Behavioral Pain Scale (BPS) tool. Then, the score of the BPS tool was compared before and after the intervention. Educational interventions included the explanation and training of the BPS tool. The explanations given included teaching the dimensions of the BPS tool, how to complete the tool and score it, the difference between the BPS tool and other conventional methods of pain assessment in the ICU department, how to interpret the results of the BPS tool, and perform palliative interventions in the field of pain control. The instruments used included the Glasgow Coma Scale, DSM-IV Scale, and BPS. Data analysis was done using SPSS16 software, t-test, and analysis of variance tests.RESULTS:The results showed that the implementation of the training program had improved the scores obtained by nurses in all three dimensions of the BPS questionnaire. In all aspects of the questionnaire, the overall pain score of the patients after the implementation of the training was higher than the score before the implementation of the training (P = 0.000). On the other hand, there was no significant difference in the score before and after the implementation of the training in the third stage of pain assessment in the mechanical ventilation dimension (P = 0.22).CONCLUSION:Considering the effect of the educational intervention on improving the pain identification score and providing palliative care in patients hospitalized in the ICU, it is suggested that a suitable educational program be included in the nursing bachelor's curriculum.

TI Mothers' experiences of implementing a normal labor and delivery
   management program based on evidence-based clinical practice in Iran
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Evidence-based clinical practice; labor; management program; natural
   childbirth
ID BIRTH
AB BACKGROUND:Natural childbirth, as a significant and impatful experience in a woman's life, can have substantial positive or negative effects on her physical and psychological well-being. Therefore, evidence-based care, which includes active labor management programs and the reduction of unnecessary medical interventions, has been recognized as an effective approach to enhance the positive experience of natural childbirth and reduce the need for cesarean sections. Therefore, this study aimed to explain mothers' experiences of implementing a normal labor and delivery management program based on evidence-based clinical practice in Iran.MATERIALS AND METHODS:This qualitative study was conducted in 2024 on 16 primiparous mothers who had experience with the normal labor and delivery management program based on evidence-based clinical practice. Women were selected through purposive sampling at Sina Hospital in Ahvaz, Iran.RESULTS:After analyzing the data, the mother's experiences were categorized into three main categories: a sense of control, the pleasantness of the childbirth process, and acceptance of natural childbirth.CONCLUSION:The implementation of evidence-based programs focusing on woman-centered care has the potential to improve the quality of childbirth care in Iran and enhance maternal satisfaction. This approach promotes a sense of security and comfort for women during labor, while empowering them to make informed decisions about their care.

TI Comparison of the effect of standardized patient-based training and
   video-based training on the skill of measuring the level of
   consciousness among nursing students: A randomized controlled trial
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Consciousness disorders; Glasgow coma scale; neurologic examination;
   simulation training; standardized patient. video-based training
AB BACKGROUND:Ensuring accurate assessment of patients' health is paramount in nursing interventions. The Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) plays a crucial role in evaluating patients' conditions and is deemed a fundamental clinical skill for nursing teams. However, errors in GCS assessment can significantly impact patient care, particularly as nursing students often lack sufficient training in assessing consciousness levels.OBJECTIVE:This study aimed to compare the effectiveness of standardized patient-based training and video-based training (VBT) on nursing students' ability to assess the level of consciousness.METHOD AND MATERIALS:This randomized controlled trial study included nursing students from the fourth semester in 2023. Seventy students were selected through convenience sampling and randomly allocated to two groups (n = 35 per group). Group 1 received VBT, while Group 2 received training with standardized patients. The skill of assessing consciousness levels was evaluated using the Objective Structured Clinical Examination method. Data analysis was performed using SPSS V22 statistical software (Statistical Package for the Social Sciences, SPSS, Chicago, IL, USA).RESULTS:The mean score of the verbal response assessment in the standardized patient-assisted education group was 3.42 +/- 0.84 and that in the video-based training (VBT) group was 2.85 +/- 1.09, which was statistically significant (P = 0.025). Additionally, the total test score was significantly higher in the standardized patient-assisted training group (13.21 +/- 1.49) compared to the VBT group (12.15 +/- 2.22) (P = 0.032).CONCLUSION:Training with standardized patients significantly improves nursing students' ability to assess consciousness levels compared to VBT. This approach aligns with health policy benchmarks by promoting safe, experiential learning methods, ultimately enhancing psychomotor skills while minimizing risks to real patients.

TI Intervention based on the family health nurse model on hypertension in
   the elderly: Protocol for a randomized clinical trial
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Elderly; family nurse; hypertension; model; self-management
AB BACKGROUND:This demographic is disproportionately affected by various health challenges, making them the primary users of healthcare resources, with hypertension being a prevalent chronic condition among them. Effective management of blood pressure can lead to a notable decrease in expenditures associated with advanced medical treatments. Among the various family-centered strategies, the family health nurse (FHN) model, proposed by the World Health Organization in 1998, stands out.MATERIALS AND METHODS:This randomized controlled clinical trial was carried out from September to March 2023 at selected healthcare institutions in Isfahan City. A random number table was used to identify 78 eligible participants for the study. The intervention group received strategies rooted in the FHN model, including personalized and family education, establishment of self-help groups, and both internal and external support follow-ups to enhance hypertension self-management. In contrast, the control group received standard care. The efficacy of the intervention was assessed using the Stanford University Chronic Disease Self-Management Questionnaire, comprising 38 questions across 8 dimensions, administered at three intervals: before the intervention, immediately post-intervention, and 3 months later, alongside blood pressure measurements.CONCLUSION:Considering that social factors, including the family, are determinants of health, determining the effectiveness of the FHN model on the control and prevention of hypertension can provide a suitable framework for providing family-oriented services to the elderly with hypertension and improving their health. By carrying out the necessary tests, information will be gathered. Software called SPSS 22 (Version 18, Isfahan, Iran) will be used for data analysis.

TI The effect of mindfulness-based intervention on mother's body image and
   maternal fetal attachment
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Attachment; body image; mindfulness; pregnancy
ID DEPRESSIVE SYMPTOMS; SELF-ESTEEM; PREGNANCY; SATISFACTION; WEIGHT;
   WOMEN; ANXIETY; STRESS; LIFE
AB BACKGROUND:Pregnancy is associated with a wide range of physiologic and psychologic changes that could affect a mother's body image and maternal-fetal attachment. One of the presented interventions regarding body image and maternal fetal attachment is mindfulness-based intervention. According to the evidence, mindfulness could be affected by various variables such as sociocultural background. Therefore, the present study was conducted to determine the effect of mindfulness-based intervention on mothers' body image and maternal fetal attachment among women who referred to the comprehensive health center of Isfahan-Iran.MATERIALS AND METHODS:The present quasi-experimental study was conducted on 70 pregnant women who were referred to the comprehensive health centers of Isfahan. The sampling method was convenient, and participants were allocated into two groups. While both groups received routine prenatal care, the intervention group also participated in a 6-session mindfulness counseling course. Demographic characteristics questionnaire, body image, and maternal fetal attachment scale were completed before and 1 month after the end of the intervention by both groups. Data were analyzed using the student t-test, Chi-square test, and Fisher's exact test.RESULTS:No significant difference was observed between the intervention and control group before (respectively, 105.3 and 103.3) and after (respectively, 106 and 105.4) the intervention regarding the score of body image. In the control group, the mean maternal-fetal attachment score did not differ significantly after the intervention compared to before (respectively, 93.6 and 93.5). However, in the intervention group, there was a significant difference between the score of attachment before and after (respectively, 93.4 and 99.06) the intervention (P = 0.004). The mean score of maternal fetal attachment after the intervention showed a significant difference (P = 0.009) between the intervention and control group (99.06 and 93.5), meaning that the mean score of maternal fetal attachment was higher in the intervention group.CONCLUSIONS:Mindfulness-based counseling was effective in the improvement of maternal fetal attachment and could be used in interventional programs related to the mental health of pregnant mothers. Also, to design interventions for improvement of body image in pregnant mothers further studies should be conducted.

TI From social capital to informal power: A qualitative exploration of
   cancer care inequalities in Morocco
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Cancer; cancer care trajectories; informal power; social capital; social
   inequalities in health
AB BACKGROUND:Cancer patients are not merely passive recipients of care. Some, especially those with extensive experience or strong engagement in their therapeutic journey, develop informal forms of influence that operate outside institutional boundaries. This study explores these dynamics by analyzing how informal power is exercised by cancer patients and how it reshapes care relationships, particularly when there is an over-reliance on personal networks to navigate formal health care systems.MATERIALS AND METHODS:This qualitative study draws on thematic analysis of clinical observations and semi-structured interviews conducted in multiple hospital settings in the Fez-Meknes region. The analysis is grounded in a sociological framework combining concepts of relational legitimacy, social capital, and empowerment to explain how informal power emerges and is recognized in care contexts.RESULTS:Patients with experiential knowledge or broad social networks often support peers, offer therapeutic advice, or mediate interactions with healthcare professionals. Though informal and non-institutionalized, this influence impacts clinical decisions, team dynamics, and patient group organization. However, access to this form of power remains unevenly distributed, reinforcing existing social inequalities.CONCLUSION:Informal patient power is a double-edged resource for health professionals. While it can foster patient autonomy and enhance clinical collaboration, it also raises ethical challenges. Institutional acknowledgment and ethical regulation-such as clear protocols, interdisciplinary mediation mechanisms, and training programs for healthcare workers-are needed to balance personal initiative with equity and organizational fairness.

TI Performance metrics in cardiac resuscitation: Rapid cycle deliberate
   practice (RCDP) versus simulated clinical experience (SCE)
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Advanced Cardiac Life Support; debriefing; deliberate practice;
   resuscitation protocol; simulation training
AB BACKGROUND:Cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) remain the leading cause of mortality globally, with sudden cardiac arrest (SCA) due to ventricular tachyarrhythmias accounting for nearly 25% of cardiovascular deaths. Effective simulation-based training is critical for improving clinical performance and outcomes in cardiac emergencies. Simulated Clinical Experience (SCE) and Rapid Cycle Deliberate Practice (RCDP) are two structured instructional methods. This study explores which method is more effective in managing cardiac arrest. To compare the effectiveness of RCDP and SCE in improving performance metrics in the management of cardiac arrhythmias.MATERIALS AND METHODS:This pre-post interventional study was conducted among healthcare professionals trained in Advanced Cardiovascular Life Support (ACLS). Participants (n = 240) were divided into two equal groups and underwent two simulation scenarios (one baseline and one post-instruction). Key metrics assessed included time to rhythm recognition, initiation of CPR, defibrillation, and identification of Return of Spontaneous Circulation (ROSC). While the SCE group received traditional post-scenario debriefing, the RCDP group underwent sessions with embedded facilitator feedback. Facilitators were blinded to group allocation during assessments.RESULTS:The RCDP group showed significantly faster response times across all measured metrics, along with reduced variability and improved Chest Compression Fractions (P value = 0.018) and ROSC identification (P value = 0.003). SCE participants demonstrated improvement, though outcomes were modest. The iterative feedback and repetitive structure of RCDP likely contributed to superior outcomes.CONCLUSION:RCDP offers measurable benefits in enhancing resuscitation performance. However, both methods contribute to skill development.

TI Melody vs. message: Effects of traditional song and concise social media
   communications on iodine knowledge, attitudes, behaviors, and biomarkers
   in pregnant women-A randomized controlled trial
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Digital media; health promotion; iodine deficiency; maternal health;
   Molum; online platforms; Thai folk song; urinary iodine excretion
AB BACKGROUND:Iodine deficiency remains a global public health problem. Urinary iodine concentration (UIC) in pregnant women is a key indicator of iodine status in the population. Knowledge (K), attitude (A), and practice (P) levels of pregnant women may influence UIC.MATERIALS AND METHODS:This study aimed to assess the impact of educational interventions on UIC and KAP scores among pregnant women. A three-arm randomized controlled trial was conducted involving 231 pregnant women divided into two intervention groups and one control group. The intervention A, B and control groups received Thai folk song, short message VDO Doctor, and standard counselling, respectively. Interventions were delivered daily via LINE for 2 weeks. Data were collected using spot urine samples and KAP questionnaires.RESULTS:At baseline, UIC and KAP scores showed no significant differences (P = 0.148 for UIC; 0.126, 0.179, 0.146 for K, A, P, respectively). After intervention, UIC levels in Thai folk song and VDO Doctor groups were not significantly higher than standard counselling (P = 0.518 and 0.855, respectively). No significant differences were found between Thai folk song and VDO Doctor in UIC (P = 0.399) or KAP scores. Within-group analysis revealed that Thai folk song significantly increased K and A scores, whilst VDO Doctor increased A scores only. UIC showed no significant changes.CONCLUSION:Results suggest Thai folk song and VDO Doctor were more effective than standard counselling for improving K and A scores, though neither intervention significantly affected P scores.

TI Comparison of the effect of eight weeks of Rhythmic aerobic training and
   CX-WORX on cholesterol transport and inflammatory factors in obese women
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE ATP binding cassette transporter; balanced aerobic exercises; CX-WORK
   exercises; follistatin; insulin-like peptides; interleukin-6; member 5;
   subfamily G
ID EXERCISE; EXPRESSION
AB BACKGROUND:Obesity is associated with a wide range of complications and an increased risk of premature occurrence of physical problems, mental disorders, and some diseases. Doing sports activities along with other treatment strategies can be an effective solution to overcome this problem. Therefore, this study aimed to compare the effect of balanced aerobic exercise and CX-WORK on the expression of growth genes, metabolic biomarkers, and indicators of reverse cholesterol transport in obese women.MATERIALS AND METHODS:In this semi-experimental study, with a pre-test-post-test design and a control group, 45 individuals with an average age of 25.47 years and a BMI between 30 and 35 kg/m2 were purposefully selected among the obese women of Isfahan City and were randomly divided to three groups of 15 individuals; Balanced aerobic exercises, CX-WORK and control exercises. Rhythmic aerobic training protocol including eight weeks, rhythmic movements accompanied by music, and three sessions of 40 to 50 min per week was implemented incrementally. The CX-WORK exercise program was performed for eight weeks, three sessions a week and each session lasted 30 min. This program was done in six stages warming up, strength and endurance movements related to central muscles 1, standing endurance movements 1, standing endurance movements 2, strength and endurance movements related to central muscles 2, and strength and endurance movements related to central muscles 3. Blood sampling was conducted to estimate the study variables and to measure height, weight, and BMI index in two stages pre-test and post-test. To test the significance of group mean differences, one-way analysis of variance and Tukey's post hoc test were used using SPSS software version 26 at a significance level of 0.05.RESULTS:The results of the study showed that in both experimental groups; The expression of GH, IGF-1, Follistatin, ABCG1, ABCG5, and ABCG8 genes increased significantly (P >= 0.05). In addition, a significant decrease was observed in both experimental groups in myostatin, IL-6, and CRP gene expression in obese women (P >= 0.05). In addition, although there was a difference between the effects of the two types of exercise on these variables, this difference was not significant (P <= 0.05).CONCLUSION:These results showed the beneficial effects of balanced aerobic exercise and CX-WORK on the expression of growth genes, metabolic biomarkers, and indicators of reverse cholesterol transport in obese women. Therefore, the use of these training methods is recommended as a suitable prevention and treatment method for obesity and improving the aforementioned indicators.

TI Change in nutrition patterns through a school-based intervention-The
   Altus health and wellness academy model
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATION AND HEALTH PROMOTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Adolescent; child; healthy lifestyle; school health services
ID VEGETABLE INTAKE; BEHAVIORS; FRUITS; ADOLESCENTS; DISEASE; YOUTH
AB BACKGROUND:Childhood and adolescent obesity continue to plague our nation. Health interventions must begin early. When students introduce more nutritious foods into their diets like fruits and vegetables, their health is positively impacted. This study reports on improvements in willingness to try new fruits and vegetables and correlated health behaviors, like physical activity, after participation in a school-based wellness program, The Health and Wellness Academy (HWA).MATERIALS AND METHODS:Seventy-two students participated in HWA, with a mean age of 10.43 +/- 2.18 years. 58.3% were female, 75% were Hispanic, and the remaining 25% were Black. Each HWA session involved tailored nutrition and physical activity interventions. Pre- and post-program surveys were utilized to obtain nutrition data.RESULTS:Results indicated that the willingness to try new fruits and new vegetables increased along with the length of time in HWA. The mixed linear model regression results revealed significant time effects on both willingness to try new fruits (P = 0.011) and willingness to try new vegetables (P = 0.001). Additionally, Spearman correlation analyses between nutritional outcomes and physical activity outcomes indicated that the relationship between different variables changed from baseline to follow-up assessments (r = 0.31, 0.48 and 0.32, with P = 0.033, 0.001, and 0.028).CONCLUSIONS:Having a consistent, sustained intervention with a dedicated nutrition team allows youth to be exposed to a variety of nutrition options. Our findings indicate the HWA's tailored model allows for youth to find nutrition that is meaningful and relevant, thus willing to try new nutritious foods.

TI Association of the naples prognostic score with revascularization
   strategies in patients with prior CABG and NSTE-ACS: A retrospective
   single-center observational study
SO SCIENCE PROGRESS
LA English
DT Article
DE coronary artery bypass grafting; non-st Elevation acute coronary
   syndrome; naples prognostic score; biomarkers; revascularization; risk
   stratification
ID ACUTE CORONARY SYNDROMES; MYOCARDIAL-INFARCTION; SAPHENOUS-VEIN;
   OUTCOMES; SURGERY
AB Objective Patients with a prior history of coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) presenting with non-ST-elevation acute coronary syndrome (NSTE-ACS) represent a high-risk population in whom revascularization decisions are frequently individualized in real-world practice. Objective biomarkers capable of supporting treatment selection in this setting remain limited. The Naples Prognostic Score (NPS), a composite index integrating inflammatory and nutritional parameters, may reflect overall clinical vulnerability. Methods In this retrospective, single-center observational cohort study, the association between NPS and treatment strategy selection was evaluated in 367 patients with prior CABG presenting with NSTE-ACS between January 2019 and October 2025. NPS was calculated at admission prior to coronary angiography using total cholesterol, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, lymphocyte-to-monocyte ratio, and serum albumin levels. Patients were categorized into low (0-2) and high (3-4) NPS groups. Treatment strategies were determined through routine multidisciplinary clinical assessment and were not influenced by study investigators. Multivariable logistic regression and prespecified stratified sensitivity analyses were performed. Results Revascularization was selected in 169 patients (46.0%), including 164 percutaneous coronary interventions and 5 redo CABG procedures. Patients undergoing revascularization had significantly lower NPS values. High NPS was independently associated with a lower likelihood of being selected for revascularization (OR 0.28, 95% CI 0.17-0.48; p < 0.001). Procedural success rates following PCI were similar between NPS groups (89.0% overall; p = 0.161). Results remained consistent across stratified sensitivity analyses according to clinical presentation, chronic kidney disease status, and age categories. Conclusions Higher NPS values were associated with a lower likelihood of revascularization without affecting procedural success. NPS appears to reflect disease burden and clinical vulnerability rather than treatment benefit. It may also capture acute inflammatory status and should be considered a complementary, not decisive, clinical marker.

TI Ultrasound-guided anteroposterior percutaneous catheter drainage for the
   treatment of psoas abscess: A case series
SO SCIENCE PROGRESS
LA English
DT Article
DE ultrasound; psoas abscess (PA); percutaneous catheter drainage (PCD);
   minimally invasive treatment (MIT); case series
ID ILIOPSOAS
AB Psoas abscess (PA) is a rare but potentially life-threatening condition that requires prompt intervention. The role of ultrasound-guided percutaneous catheter drainage (US-PCD) via the anterior-posterior (AP) approach warrants further evaluation. This case series retrospectively analyzed 10 patients with PA who underwent US-guided AP-PCD at Beijing Friendship Hospital. Data collected included procedure duration, pre- and postoperative clinical examinations, inflammatory markers, and imaging findings. Technical success was achieved in all cases (median procedure time: 18.5 minutes). Postprocedural Visual Analog Scale (VAS) pain scores decreased within 24 hours. By postoperative day 3, eight patients had normalized body temperature and white blood cell (WBC) counts. Median C-reactive protein (CRP) levels decreased from 151.3 mg/L (range: 58.0-269.4) preoperatively to 49.5 mg/L (range:38.7-186.1) postoperatively. During a follow-up period of 1-6 months, six patients achieved clinical success without further intervention, two required surgical debridement, and two died. This case series demonstrates that US-guided AP-PCD represents a feasible and safe minimally invasive option for selected patients with PA, offering the advantages of real-time guidance and no radiation exposure. However, given the modest success rate (60%) and etiological heterogeneity of this cohort, larger prospective studies are needed to validate its clinical role.

TI Exploring Participant Perspectives on Implementation and Sustainment of
   Taking It to the Pews: A Faith-Based HIV Intervention With African
   American Churches
SO AIDS EDUCATION AND PREVENTION
LA English
DT Article
DE African Americans; faith-based organizations; churches; HIV edu cation;
   HIV testing; focus groups
ID PUBLIC-HEALTH; BLACK CHURCH; HIV/AIDS; PREVENTION; MINISTRY; BARRIERS;
   STIGMA; CARE; OPPORTUNITIES; INVOLVEMENT
AB African American faith institutions can play a key role in increasing HIV education and testing in communities disproportionately burdened by HIV. This focus group study explored church participant perspectives of a religiously tailored HIV education and testing intervention implemented through a clustered, randomized controlled trial with 14 African American churches in Kansas City. Focus group participants from intervention churches emphasized the importance of churches providing access to HIV screening/education and support for people with HIV. They noted that pastors' involvement (e.g., integrating messages into sermons, publicly getting tested) encouraged others to get tested. TIPS materials were seen as easy to understand, and the intervention fostered more HIV discussions and partnerships with public health organizations. Challenges included time demands and limited church staff. Participants recommended stronger connections among intervention churches for support and idea sharing. Overall, religiously tailored HIV education and testing interventions are highly acceptable when supported by trusted faith and public health partnerships.

TI An Evidence-Based Approach to Facilitating PrEP Initiation Among YMSM:
   The MyPEEPS Plus mHealth and E-Peer Navigation Intervention
SO AIDS EDUCATION AND PREVENTION
LA English
DT Article
DE PrEP; peer navigation; mHealth; HIV; YMSM; youth
ID PREEXPOSURE PROPHYLAXIS; HIV PREVENTION; SOCIAL DETERMINANTS; YOUNG MEN;
   SEX; RISK; HEALTH; TOOL
AB Men who have sex with men (MSM) account for nearly 70% of new HIV infections annually. Although awareness of pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) is growing, uptake remains low among young MSM. Peer navigators are well positioned to guide patients through PrEP care, provide psychosocial support, build trust, and demystify PrEP. Given strong evidence to support mobile health (mHealth) apps for enhancing HIV prevention knowledge, our team created MyPEEPS Plus, a HIV prevention combination intervention of mHealth and an electronic peer (e-peer) navigation program. In this article, we describe development of a remote intervention that incorporates evidence-based strategies including: HIV Incidence Risk Index for Men Who Have Sex With Men (HIRI-MSM); open-ended questions, affirmations, reflective listening, and summarizing (OARS); shared decision making approach; the PrEP Readiness Assessment (PRA); and motivational interviewing (MI) for use in an RCT. By combining digital education with personalized support, MyPEEPS Plus is designed to empower youth and reduce barriers to PrEP initiation and persistence.

TI Understanding How Information Sources Shape Perceptions of HIV Among
   Adolescents and Young Adults (AYA) in Tajikistan: A Qualitative Study
SO AIDS EDUCATION AND PREVENTION
LA English
DT Article
DE adolescents and young adults; HIV prevention; HIV education; Central
   Asia; Tajikistan
ID RISK BEHAVIORS; PREVENTION; PEOPLE; IMMUNIZATION; KNOWLEDGE; KAZAKSTAN;
   HIV/AIDS; SCHOOL; MEDIA; YOUTH
AB Adolescents and young adults (AYA) aged 15-24 in Tajikistan have the Europe and Central Asia; however, little research has explored what sources of HIV information they utilize. We conducted a qualitative study with 36 AYA in Dushanbe, grouped by gender and age. Participants engaged in participatory activities and discussions over two sessions. We conducted thematic analysis and identified three main themes: (1) school-based HIV education was limited and technical, leaving practical knowledge gaps; (2) social networks often spread inaccurate, stigmatizing information; and (3) AYA preferred professional sources but had limited access, relying instead on potentially inaccurate sources like social media. Tajik AYA lack information sources which empower them with accurate information and build their capacity to engage in preventive behaviors. Educational efforts must move beyond knowledge enhancement to address social and structural barriers to information sharing regarding HIV.

TI Awareness, Acceptability, and Preferences for Pre-exposure Prophylaxis
   Modalities Among Black Women: A Critical Review and Brief Report of a
   Pilot Study
SO AIDS EDUCATION AND PREVENTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Black women; HIV prevention; pre-exposure prophylaxis; long-acting
   injectable PrEP; modality preferences; multipurpose prevention
   technology
ID UNITED-STATES; REPRODUCTIVE HEALTH; PREP; ATTITUDES; KNOWLEDGE; RACISM;
   EXPERIENCE; RISK
AB Black women experience a disproportionate burden of human immunodeficiency virus in the United States, yet use of pre-exposure prophylaxis remains low. This article critically reviews published research on barriers to and facilitators of pre-exposure prophylaxis acceptability among Black women and presents findings from a qualitative pilot study examining awareness and preferences for available and emerging prevention modalities. A critical review of 50 peer-reviewed studies published between 2012 and 2025 identified persistent challenges as well as facilitators. The pilot study included focus groups and interviews with 20 pre-exposure prophylaxis- na & iuml;ve Black women in two high-incidence Texas counties. Participants demonstrated limited awareness of injectable prevention options, varied preferences across modalities, and strong interest in expanded delivery settings such as pharmacies, mobile services, and at-home options. Findings indicate that low uptake reflects structural gaps in prevention systems rather than lack of interest, underscoring the need for diversified modalities and accessible delivery models.

TI Design, Implementation, and Pilot Evaluation of the Save Yourself Board
   Game as a Game-Based Science Communication Intervention for HIV/AIDS
   Awareness Among University Students
SO AIDS EDUCATION AND PREVENTION
LA English
DT Article
DE game-based learning; HIV/AIDS education; board game; stigma-related
   awareness; science communication; pilot study; thematic analysis
AB This pilot study introduces Save Yourself, an educational board game designed to teach HIV/AIDS biology and prevention, enhance science communication, and reduce stigma. Using a single-group pretest/posttest design, 42 university students (M-age = 24.6) completed a 20-item HIV/AIDSknowledge quiz, evaluation items, and open-ended feedback. Paired samples t tests revealed significant knowledge gains (pre: M = 64.97%, SD = 9.77; post: M = 85.10%, SD = 7.86; t(41) = -10.68, p < .001, d = -1.65), with large improvements in transmission and prevention subscales. Descriptive ratings were high for gameplay, clarity, and mechanics (approximate to 4.5/5). A binomial test showed 81% of participants felt the game addressed stigma (p < .001). Thematic analysis identified seven areas for improvement, including balance of fun and learning, clarity of instructions, and social impact. Measurement issues emerged, as the Educational Game Scale showed poor reliability (alpha = -.04). Overall, Save Yourself shows promise as a low-tech, engaging HIV/AIDS education tool.

TI Succession planning in liquid modernity: an interdisciplinary analysis
   of sociocultural paradigms and their implications
SO ECCOS-REVISTA CIENTIFICA
LA English
DT Article
DE succession law; liquid modernity; paradigm shift; succession planning;
   sociology
AB This study examines succession planning as a response to the sociocultural transformations of modernity, focusing on paradigm shifts and their implications. Adopting an interdisciplinary framework spanning Law, Sociology, and Philosophy, this research investigates the sociocultural shifts that shape contemporary attitudes toward death, inheritance, and succession. Furthermore, it demonstrates the effectiveness of succession planning as a legal-economic instrument for asset transfer and to understand sociocultural and paradigmatic mutations through the sociological lens of Zygmunt Bauman and the philosophical framework proposed by Thomas Kuhn. The methodology used qualitative and exploratory bibliographic research, with a cross-sectional design and dialectical method. Findings reveal a marked increase in the demand for succession-planning mechanisms, particularly during COVID-19 pandemic, which accentuated the precariousness of life and the fluidity of interpersonal relationships. The study concludes that succession planning constitutes a vital strategy for ensuring legal certainty and safeguarding family assets as a vital strategy for legal and property security in a society marked by individualization, instability, and volatility.

TI A simulator for LED photoreactors: Integrating light-matter interaction
   modelling and intrinsic kinetic studies for chemical engineering
   education
SO EDUCATION FOR CHEMICAL ENGINEERS
LA English
DT Article
DE Chemical Engineering Education; Simulator; LEDs; Light-matter
   interaction; Local Superficial Rate of Photon Absorption
ID HETEROGENEOUS PHOTOCATALYSIS; VIRTUAL LABORATORIES; CATALYSIS; REACTORS;
   SCIENCE
AB The incorporation of virtual tools has been shown to enhance comprehension and engagement in chemical engineering education. To support practical learning in photocatalytic reactor design, the LEDsModel Lab simulator was developed in MATLAB (R) R2024b and fully compatible with GNU Octave (version 9.2.0), focusing on the determination of the Local Superficial Rate of Photon Absorption (LSRPA) and the influence of reactor configuration on light distribution. Through four case studies, students apply theoretical models to practical scenarios, bridging the gap between theory and practice. Fully integrated into the Advanced Analysis and Design of Chemical Reactors course (6 ECTS, Master's in Chemical Engineering, University of Granada), preliminary classroom observations indicate a positive trend in student performance, accompanied by increased engagement with photocatalytic reactor modelling. This is reflected in higher grades and lower failure rates, alongside a clear strengthening of key competencies in problem-solving, quantitative analysis, and computational modelling. Its implementation has further allowed an expansion of course content to include intrinsic photocatalytic kinetics, demonstrating the potential of interactive simulation tools to enrich curriculum content, improve learning outcomes, and prepare students for the analytical and practical challenges of modern chemical engineering.

TI A Rhetoric of Exhaustion: Dialect, Labour and Critical Literacy for
   Policy and Curriculum
SO JOURNAL FOR CRITICAL EDUCATION POLICY STUDIES
LA English
DT Article
DE exhaustion-as-method; dialect epistemic voice; labour poetics;
   linguistic justice; critical language awareness
AB This article reinterprets Samuel Laycocks''Th'Shurat Weavers'Song' (1863) as a historically grounded instance of a rhetoric of exhaustion, in which bodily depletion is converted into aesthetic method and vernacular critique. Bringing together cultural materialism, Freirean critical literacy, labour poetics scholarship and language ideology theory, the analysis shows how dialectal density, rhythmic drag, patterned repetition and tonal hybridity formalise industrial fatigue under the conditions of the Lancashire Cotton Famine. A compact comparison with Ellen Johnston, Ernest Jones clarifies Laycocks' distinctive synthesis of testimonial immediacy, political address and dialectal realism. The article argues that dialect functions as epistemic voice, challenging standard language hierarchies and offering a historical model for linguistic justice in education. Policy implications follow for dialect affirming assessment, curriculum design informed by labour poetics and teacher education oriented to critical language awareness. Finally, the study gestures to Eco pedagogy, reading Laycocks'material focus on Surat cotton as an early trace of eco social entanglements between labour exhaustion and degraded ecologies. By recentring a working-class poet within nineteenth century literary culture, the article contributes a transferable analytic-exhaustion as method-that links Victorian labour poetics to current struggles over democratic pedagogy, collective agency and equitable curriculum formation.

TI Teaching as an Ideal Career Choice for Women: Reasons and Gender Roles
   behind being `ideal' and `choice'
SO JOURNAL FOR CRITICAL EDUCATION POLICY STUDIES
LA English
DT Article
DE gender roles; feminization of teaching; career choices; critical
   education; teaching in Turkiye
AB Gender, as a socially and culturally constructed phenomenon rather than a purely biological distinction, shapes career choices and sustains occupational segregation that limits women's social mobility. In this context, gendered patterns in higher education preferences constitute a critical issue, as they reflect and reproduce unequal power relations and social norms that restrict individuals' access to educational opportunities based on gender, thereby undermining equality of opportunity in education. Accordingly, this study critically examines how gender influence female students' higher education preferences in faculties of education in Turkiye, situating these choices within the broader context of educational inequality and the reproduction of patriarchal norms. In the research, phenomenology, one of the qualitative research designs, was utilized, and the study group consisted of undergraduate students determined with purposeful sampling techniques in accordance with the qualitative research. The data were collected using semi-structured interview form prepared by the researchers after expert opinions and pilot interview, and then were analysed with content analysis. The findings demonstrated how deeply embedded gender expectations, reinforced by family, school, and societal discourses, channel women into caregiving professions such as teaching. This process illustrates how education systems function as microcosms of broader gender regimes, legitimizing existing social relations while constraining women's professional agency. The article argues for gender-transformative reforms that challenge the ideological and structural mechanisms of inequality, ensuring that women's academic success translates into genuine professional and socioeconomic empowerment.

TI Allocation, Inequity, and Accountability-A Social Justice Analysis of
   Federal School Improvement Policy
SO JOURNAL FOR CRITICAL EDUCATION POLICY STUDIES
LA English
DT Article
DE School Improvement; K-12 education Policy; Resource Allocation;
   Education Policy; Critical Education Policy; Title I; and Critical Race
   Theory
AB This study examines how state education agencies (SEAs) make funding decisions to support schools identified for comprehensive support and improvement under section 1003a of the Every Student Succeeds Act (ESSA). Despite the federal mandate that states reserve and strategically deploy Title I Part A funds for school improvement, little is known about the mechanisms through which SEAs translate that mandate into practice. Drawing on semi-structured interviews with ten SEA administrators across geographically and demographically diverse sates, supplemented by document analysis of publicly available policy materials from California and New York, this study investigates two research questions: how SEAs determine funding levels for school improvement, and what criteria they apply when reviewing district applications. Thematic analysis of the data revealed four interconnected findings: 1) SEAs rely predominantly on enrollment-based and flat base allocation formulas that are structurally indifferent to school level need; 2) several states lack coherent or documented funding processes altogether; 3) funding decisions in multiple states are anchored to historical practices-including prior-year carryover-rather than differentiated need assessments; and 4) application review processes, even when formally elaborate, function as compliance mechanisms rather than instruments for equity-intentional resource distribution. The findings carry implications for federal oversight of Section 1003a, state-level SEA capacity investment, and the redesign of application processes as instruments of needs-based, funding determination.

TI Evaluation of the Distance Education Experiences of Tourism Guidance
   Department Students and Academic Staff in the Context of Critical
   Pedagogy
SO JOURNAL FOR CRITICAL EDUCATION POLICY STUDIES
LA English
DT Article
DE Critical pedagogy; equality of opportunity in education; dialogic
   learning; tourism education
AB The purpose of this study is to examine the experiences of tourism guidance department students in Turkey during the pandemic (COVID-19) process and the distance education process following the earthquake on February 6, 2023, in the context of critical pedagogy's characteristics of equal opportunity and dialogic learning. Using a descriptive phenomenological research design, data were collected from 15 academic staff working at universities in different regions of Turkey and 27 students studying at these universities through semi-structured interviews. The research findings show that students and academic staff experienced significant physical and infrastructural challenges during the distance education process, that inequality of opportunity was reproduced, and that dialogic learning disappeared. The research results were interpreted in the context of critical pedagogy's characteristics of equal opportunity and dialogic learning, and the validity of using the distance education model was discussed.
